mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 exceeding 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives lower equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market that pushes wage inflation higher, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise rates and reducing corporate profit margins, which in turn leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in INDPRO below 98 for three consecutive months indicates a contraction in industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in RSAFS below the 10th percentile for the prior year indicates a tightening monetary policy coupled with reduced household savings, which constrains consumer spending and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with weak household balance sheets
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below zero.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in HOUST and GDPC1 above their respective 3-month moving averages signals improving housing demand and broader economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered episodes compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in PAYEMS below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions and reduced consumer purchasing power, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below zero.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent CPIAUCSL above 3.5% for six consecutive months signals embedded inflation above the Fed's target, which increases the probability of sustained higher interest rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
